Written life first, then interpreted by a separate response author without the engine or results. These are synthetic checks. There is no correct career answer key.

Life from age 4 to 16

I like a good argument when everyone understands the rules and can change their mind. I also like sewing something with my hands after all that talking, because a finished seam does not need another paragraph of explanation.

  • family: Lives with parents, grandmother, and two brothers; aunt lives in Garland, Texas.
  • finances: Moderate income with a shared education savings plan.
  • geography: St. Paul, Minnesota.
  • cultureLanguages: Somali and English; Muslim family with active community relationships.
  • school: Public high school with strong humanities electives and an after-school game club.
  • accessOpportunities: Libraries, recreation programs, and family lodging for Texas visits.
  • Age 4–5

    In 2014, Amina liked building blanket tunnels with her brothers and telling anyone who entered that they needed a reason for their journey. She was more interested in their explanations than in defending the tunnel itself.

  • Age 6–7

    At six, she began reading folktales with her grandmother. During 2017, she also learned simple hand stitches, enjoying the repeated motions while asking why stories from different books sometimes gave the same action opposite moral meanings.

  • Age 8–9

    In 2018, Amina discovered strategy games and became fascinated by rules that encouraged cooperation. She often changed a game after losing, then learned that other players wanted to agree to any changes before starting the next round.

  • Age 10–11

    During 2020, she used online games to keep friendships going and helped her grandmother make video calls. She enjoyed teaching technology when questions were specific but became impatient when instructions were ignored or several people spoke at once.

  • Age 12–13

    At twelve, Amina joined a school discussion group and was surprised by how much she liked defending an argument she did not personally hold. In 2023, she started writing short reflections on fairness in fictional worlds.

  • Age 14–15

    Across 2024 and 2025, she sewed costume accessories for friends and helped run game-club sessions. A new member’s confusion prompted her to rewrite the introduction, and she found designing a clear explanation more interesting than winning that afternoon.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen in 2026, Amina is exploring a Texas college humanities workshop near her aunt and a local design camp. She is curious about difficult ideas but does not yet know whether she likes prolonged academic writing as much as lively discussion.

Life now

  • enjoys: Strategy games · Ethical puzzles · Hand sewing
  • avoids: Rules changed without agreement · Conversations where nobody can finish a thought
  • activities: Game club · Costume accessories · Discussion group
  • demonstratedSkills: Explains complex rules · Notices inconsistent arguments · Careful hand stitching
  • unfamiliarActivities: Long research essays · Residential programs
  • motivations: Fair participation · Intellectual play · Making ideas tangible
  • ambitions: Try extended study with unfamiliar peers · She imagines an adult life with a close community, travel to relatives, and time for games and difficult conversations.
  • struggles: Impatience with repetitive questions · Drafting longer essays
  • supports: Family · Humanities teacher · Game-club adviser · Texas aunt
  • practicalConstraints: Out-of-state travel · Shared household computer times

Still uncertain: Will sustained writing become rewarding with a topic she chooses? · How does she respond when a fair process still produces an outcome she dislikes?
